Lemma
[A Nonvanishing Top Form Orients the Space]

If $\omega $ is a nonzero alternating $n$-form on an $n$-dimensional real vector space, it determines the orientation whose positive bases $b$ satisfy $\omega (b)>0$.

Proof

\sketch Write $\omega =\omega (b)\det _b$ for any basis $b$. Its ray agrees with the orientation of $b$ exactly when $\omega (b)>0$.

□
